nahhas-irab:1-2.t:
The most correct thing said about its meaning is that the meaning is: rivalry in increase distracted you from obedience to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, until you came to the graves and were buried. This verse indicates the punishment of the grave — not what comes after it — كَلَّا سَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ (3), i.e., when you come to the graves. It is narrated from Zirr, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him: ألهاكم التكاثر was revealed concerning the punishment of the grave, and he recited up to كَلَّا سَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ (3). Al-Farrāʾ said:
The singular of المقابر is maqbara and maqbura, and some of the people of the Ḥijāz say maqbira; and I have heard mashraqa, mashruqa and mashriqa.

nahhas-irab:3-4.t:
ثُمَّ كَلَّا سَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ (4) is repetition according to al-Farrāʾ. Better than that is what al-Ḍaḥḥāk said; he said:
The first is for the disbelievers; and he held that the second is for the disobedient among the believers.

nahhas-irab:5-6.t:
كَلَّا لَوْ تَعْلَمُونَ عِلْمَ الْيَقِينِ (5): (علم) is a maṣdar (verbal noun), and the answer of لو is omitted. The implied form is: if you knew that you will see Hell, you would not have vied in increase in this world with wealth and other things. Al-Kisāʾī said: the answer of لَوْ is at the beginning of the sūra, i.e., if you knew with the knowledge of certainty, rivalry in increase would not have distracted you. Al-Kisāʾī read لَتَرَوُنَّ with ḍamma on the tāʾ — Abū ʿUbayd reported it from him. And it was read before Ibrāhīm ibn Mūsā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Jahm, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, that he read لَتَرَوُنَّ الْجَحِيمَ ثُمَّ لَتَرَوُنَّها, the first with ḍamma on the tāʾ and the second with fatḥa [Translator's note: the printed vowelling shows fatḥa in both places; the reading described is لَتُرَوُنَّ for the first]. Abū Jaʿfar said:
The preferable (reading) for the first, according to al-Farrāʾ and Abū ʿUbayd, is with fatḥa, because the repetition should be in agreement. Abū Jaʿfar said:
The better view is that it is not repetition, and that the meaning is: you will surely see Hell at the standing-place of the Resurrection.

nahhas-irab:7-7.t: ثُمَّ لَتَرَوُنَّها, when you enter the Fire. عَيْنَ الْيَقِينِ is a maṣdar (verbal noun), because the meaning is "you will surely witness it with eyewitnessing".

nahhas-irab:8-8.t: It has been said: i.e., about the bliss that distracts from obedience to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. The apparent sense of the speech indicates that it is general, and that a person is asked about every bliss he enjoyed in this world: from where he acquired it, what he intended by it, and whether he did something when another thing was more fitting than it. The ḥadīths from the Prophet ﷺ and his Companions support the apparent sense, as was read before Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn Ḥafṣ, from Yūsuf ibn Mūsā, who said: Hishām ibn ʿAbd al-Malik narrated to us, saying: Ḥammād ibn Salama narrated to us, saying: ʿAmmār ibn Abī ʿAmmār narrated to us, saying: I heard Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh say: The Prophet ﷺ came to me, and we brought out — or we offered him — fresh dates or unripe dates and water, and he said: «This is part of the bliss about which you will be asked». And ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn narrated to us, from al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad, who said: Dāwūd ibn Mihrān narrated to us, from Dāwūd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAytham [Translator's note: so in the text], from Ibn ʿAbbās: ثم لَتُسْئَلُنَّ يَوْمَئِذٍ عَنِ النَّعِيمِ, he said: security and health.
